    Estimate inverse-probability exposure weights

    Source: R/causal-weighting.R
    epi_propensity_weights.Rd

    Fits a logistic propensity score model for binary exposure and returns individual inverse-probability weights for the average treatment effect (ATE). Unstabilized weights are 1/p for exposed and 1/(1-p) for unexposed individuals. Stabilized weights replace the numerator with the corresponding observed marginal exposure probability. No trimming or clipping is performed. A warning flags extreme fitted propensities; it does not prove adequate overlap when absent. Assess balance, overlap and influential weights before interpreting results.

    Usage

    epi_propensity_weights(.data, exposure, adjust = c(), stabilized = TRUE)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame of independent individuals.

    exposure

    Binary 0/1 exposure column.

    adjust

    Tidy selection of complete numeric, factor, or logical baseline covariate columns. Defaults to an intercept-only model.

    stabilized

    Whether to calculate stabilized ATE weights.

    Value

    Input tibble with propensity and ipw columns. Fitted propensities must lie strictly between zero and one.

    Details

    A causal interpretation requires consistency, no unmeasured confounding, positivity, correct treatment-model specification, pre-exposure covariates, and suitable missingness and censoring assumptions. The function supports only complete data, main effects and linear numeric covariates, and does not account for cluster sampling or time-varying treatment. The returned weights alone do not estimate an effect or uncertainty.

    Examples

    d <- expand.grid(e = 0:1, age = 20:24, rep = 1:6)
d$y <- as.integer(d$rep <= 1 + d$e + (d$age %% 2))
weighted <- epi_propensity_weights(d, e, adjust = age)
epi_weighted_effect(weighted, e, y, ipw)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   risk_unexposed risk_exposed risk_difference risk_ratio ess_unexposed
#>            <dbl>        <dbl>           <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1          0.233          0.4           0.167       1.71            30
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: ess_exposed <dbl>, n <int>
